disclaimer: Animal Vision is a research-informed interpretive visualization. Animal perception is far more complex than can be reproduced on a human display.
privacyNote: Processed locally. Your photographs are never uploaded.

species.habitat: Woodland edges, fields, and cover where escape routes matter.
species.visionSummary: Dichromatic vision with muted red–green separation, stronger relative blue sensitivity, broad peripheral awareness, and excellent motion detection — with lower fine-detail resolution than typical human vision.

colorSensitivity.summary: Two cone types; red and green are poorly distinguished; blues remain relatively useful.
notes: Red and green hues are compressed toward a more muted palette.
Blue wavelengths are gently emphasized relative to warm reds.

fieldOfView.summary: Wide peripheral awareness suited to scanning cover and escape routes.
fieldOfView.notes: A mild soft periphery suggests breadth of awareness without claiming a true panoramic recreation.

species.motionSensitivity: High — motion often matters more than fine static detail.
species.visualAcuity: Lower fine-detail resolution than humans; softens high-frequency texture slightly.
educationalNotes: This interpretation compresses red–green differences to suggest dichromatic woodland vision.
Fine detail is softened because deer acuity is generally coarser than human foveal vision.
A soft periphery hints at wide awareness; it is not a measured field-of-view simulation.
Motion sensitivity cannot be shown in a still photograph.
cannotRepresent: True panoramic field of view on a flat display
Any claim of “seeing as a deer sees”

species.habitat: Flower-rich meadows, gardens, and woodland edges.
species.visionSummary: Trichromatic vision shifted toward ultraviolet and blue-green, with reduced usefulness of deep reds. Compound eyes cannot be accurately reproduced on a camera image.

colorSensitivity.summary: UV-sensitive in life; ordinary photographs contain no ultraviolet channel.
notes: This mode is a UV-inspired interpretive view — not recovered UV data.
Reds are reduced; blues and violets are emphasized to suggest a shifted floral palette.

fieldOfView.summary: Compound-eye mosaics are not simulated; that would invent structure the photo does not contain.
fieldOfView.notes: We avoid hexagonal overlays that invent optical artifacts.

species.motionSensitivity: High for floral approach cues; still frames cannot convey flicker fusion.
species.visualAcuity: Different spatial sampling than vertebrate eyes; we keep the photograph intact and only remap tone and color.
educationalNotes: Labeled UV-inspired because camera RGB has no ultraviolet channel to recover.
Red attenuation and blue emphasis suggest a floral world shifted away from human reds.
Subtle edge emphasis hints at pattern detection on petals — not compound-eye facets.
Never treat this as an actual UV photograph.

species.habitat: Forest floor — leaf litter, moss, logs, and damp microhabitats.
species.visionSummary: Comparatively rich color vision for a reptile, experienced from an extremely low viewing height with emphasis on nearby textures and warm forest-floor relationships.

colorSensitivity.summary: Warm, earthy color relationships with useful discrimination among greens, browns, and soft reds of leaf litter.
notes: Local texture contrast is enhanced for moss, leaves, and bark.

fieldOfView.summary: Ground-level framing matters more than panoramic width.
fieldOfView.notes: The transform emphasizes near-field texture rather than inventing a new camera angle.

species.motionSensitivity: Slow exploratory movement; still images favor texture over chase cues.
species.visualAcuity: Nearby detail is prioritized; distant haze is slightly softened.
educationalNotes: Warmth and local contrast suggest forest-floor reading of leaves, moss, and logs.
Near-field sharpening emphasizes textures a low observer might attend to.
Distant softness hints at focus on nearby ground — not a measured depth of field.
True eye height would require a different photograph; we do not invent a new camera position.
cannotRepresent: Actual turtle eye height unless the photo was already made that way
Chemosensory or tactile cues that accompany exploration
